The image presents two line graphs that illustrate the relationship between the IMF Fiscal Index and debt quotes for the overall state and central state from 1995 to 2020. Both graphs share the same x-axis, representing the years from 1995 to 2020 with a linear scale and tick labels at five-year intervals. The left y-axis represents the IMF Fiscal Index, ranging from 0 to 2.5 with a linear scale and tick labels at 0.5 intervals, while the right y-axis represents the debt quote with different scales for the overall state (60-120) and central state (30-70).

The top graph displays three lines: a blue solid line representing the overall state's debt quote, a purple solid line representing the IMF Fiscal Index is not correct as per the data, instead it is representing another debt quote, and blue dotted triangles representing the IMF Fiscal Index. The blue line starts at around 0.2 in 1995, fluctuates until 2015, and then sharply declines to approximately -0.5 in 2020. The purple line begins at around 0.2 in 1995, follows a similar pattern to the blue line until 2015, and then increases to around 0.25 in 2020. The blue dotted triangles start at around 0.2 in 1995 and steadily rise to approximately 1 by 2020.

The bottom graph also displays three lines with similar representations. The blue line starts at around -0.25 in 1995, decreases until 2006, and then sharply declines to approximately -0.75 in 2010 before rising and falling again to around -0.75 in 2020. The purple line begins at around -0.25 in 1995, follows a similar pattern to the blue line, and ends at around 0 in 2020. The blue dotted triangles start at around 0 in 1995 and steadily rise to approximately 1 by 2020.

Both graphs illustrate the trend of the IMF Fiscal Index and debt quotes over time, with the top graph focusing on the overall state and the bottom graph on the central state.
